articles.title: Dominic Calvert-Lewis: Leeds striker signs new deal until 2029 with Premier League club
articles.summary: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal until the summer of 2029 at Leeds; the striker joined the club in 2025 from Everton; he has scored six goals in all competitions this season; his form earned him a recall to the England squad
articles.body:
Sky Sports News has been reporting that he was expected to commit his future to the club, which has now been confirmed.

Manchester United had shown interest in the 29-year-old.

Calvert-Lewin joined Leeds on a free transfer in the summer of 2025 after leaving Everton. He scored 15 goals across all competitions last season, and has scored six this season. He scored in a 4-1 win against Chelsea on Saturday.

Since he joined Leeds, Calvert-Lewin is the highest-scoring Englishman in the Premier League (19) - three ahead of his next closest countrymen, Morgan Gibbs-White and Ollie Watkins.

His form for Leeds saw him return to the England set-up in March, and he also featured in the September/October and November squads. Calvert-Lewin was not selected for the World Cup.

Ao Tanaka is also close to signing a new contract with Leeds, Sky Sports News understands.

The midfielder is understood to have agreed terms on a deal that will keep him at Elland Road until 2029. The 28-year-old's current contract was due to expire in the summer of 2028.

Tanaka has grown to become a key figure in Daniel Farke's side this season, starting in nine of Leeds' 11 Premier League matches. They have lost just 10 of the 66 games Tanaka has started since then.

Calvert-Lewin follows in the footsteps of Ethan Ampadu, Joe Rodon, Jayden Bogle and Brenden Aaronson, who all signed new deals in the summer. Leeds are also reportedly set to trigger Lukas Nmecha's one-year extension.

Leeds are seventh in the Premier League, four points from the Champions League places. They face Coventry next in the league on Saturday.

Ahead of the weekend's match, Daniel Farke has refused to shed any more light on his own new contract talks. He signed a four-year contract when appointed in 2023 and that is set to expire at the end of the season.

He was reported to have parted company with his agent in October while reaching an agreement with Leeds in principle to extend his contract until 2029.

Farke said: "I'm the manager of Leeds United. I sign players. I don't sign managers. Since I've been here, I fell in love with the people here, and I fell in love with the club.

"And the only thing I care for is our supporters because they had to suffer really for such a long time. I want to bring success to them. I care for the players, I care for the staff and this is the way I work.

"I think this is also the reason I don't like to talk about my contract at all because I have to lead the people here.

"I'm a leader of men and women at this club and and no one wants a leader who talks about his future, about himself, or whatever. And this also not my style."

articles.title: Scottish FA summit: Governing body to deliver new plan for youth development as SPFL vote delayed
articles.summary: The Scottish FA will continue to consult with SPFL clubs about youth development after initial plans failed to reach a member vote.
articles.body:
At a summit in September, Scottish football's governing body proposed financial incentives and penalties along with quotas , in a bid to get more homegrown talent playing for Scottish clubs.

Initially, the plans were to have been voted on at an SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's annual meeting this month.

But the SFA are now aiming to put refreshed proposals to the clubs early in the new year, with the plan to implement them for the start of the 2027-28 season.

Despite being "encouraged", the governing body added that "recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation."

"The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews," a Scottish FA statement read.

"We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game."

"It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams."

At their initial consultation with clubs, the SFA put forward three proposals:

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Scottish Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players start in all Premier Sports Cup matches, with one player on the pitch at all times.

Clubs should field Scotland-eligible Under-21 players for an average of 60 minutes in each game across all four SPFL divisions

articles.title: Simone Magill: What will returning captain bring to Northern Ireland?
articles.summary: As she gears up for her international return, what will Simone Magill bring to Northern Ireland against Greece in Friday's friendly?
articles.body:
After 13 months away, Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute in Birmingham City's WSL defeat by Manchester United on Sunday.

It was a moment that had been a long time coming for the 31-year-old, who gave birth to her daughter, Skye, in May and has been building towards stepping back on the pitch.

Now, she will hope to make her international return with Northern Ireland in a friendly against Greece on Friday.

"It's been some time since I've been here in a playing capacity, so it's really nice just to be back in the mix again," NI captain Magill told BBC Sport NI.

"I officially made my comeback at the weekend and it was really nice to have done that. I'm really looking forward to doing that here at home in front of the fans and my family as well."

'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist'

Greece friendlies an opportunity to build - Andrews

In an interview with BBC Sport in October, Magill spoke about how being both a mum and a footballer can "co-exist".

While she was not ready to play any role in the matches, Magill, Skye and her husband Mark were all in camp for the World Cup play-off with Portugal last month, all with an eye of integrating into international duty as a family.

Having played just a handful of minutes, Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle said that while he was "delighted" to have Magill back, how much she plays across the double-header would be in collaboration with Birmingham and his captain.

"With the circumstances around this one, I'm very mindful that I need to build accordingly and I really need to listen to myself as well," Magill added.

"To even be back in this capacity this soon after giving birth, for me, is just unbelievable.

"I have no major expectations. I'm just really happy to be here and be a part of it, and if I do come on, that'll be even better."

Watch live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website

Friday's match against Greece will be Northern Ireland's first friendly in three years.

The sides will then play again on Tuesday at 16:00 GMT, and both matches can be streamed live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website.

The matches will act as preparation for the Nations League campaign in February, when Northern Ireland face tricky tests in the form of Poland, Finland and Belarus.

McArdle is developing a young squad and Magill says she hopes to bring "leadership and experience to really help us all move forward".

"We've obviously had a transition in the last year whilst I've been out, it's been nice to come back in and just feel where we're at, get on the grass with the girls and see, 'how can I help, what can I bring?'," she added.

"I'm very much looking forward to just getting back in the mix and helping try to bring the young players forward, use that experience and let's hold on to the ball, let's get into the final third, let's have a go, be brave - all of the attributes that we're known for.

"We're an underdog nation, so it's getting that across to the younger members in the squad to say, 'let's have a go with these teams and not be afraid'."

In her absence over the past year, Northern Ireland have used a number of different options in the centre forward role.

Winger Lauren Wade has shown her versatility by playing centrally, while Kess Elmore and Cora Chambers have also played up top.

Along with Magill, Portsmouth striker Kerry Beattie is also back in the squad to bolster McArdle's striking options.

"We've loads of young ones snapping at my heels. It's great, that's what we want.

"I feel we're more competitive now than ever. You never know who's going to be coming into the squad. Certainly, in more recent years, you kind of knew the squad every single time, whereas that's not the case now.

"We've got some exciting youth coming through, so it's their time now to shine."

Magill added that Northern Ireland are "heading in a new direction" ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, and the friendlies with Greece give an opportunity for the team to grow in a pressure-free environment.

"We're coming into a brand new campaign and it's really nice that we have a friendly window just now.

"We haven't had one in a very, very long time, so this is a brilliant opportunity to get us all back together, get the new faces in, get some more experience, learn things, try things.

"I'm really excited about where we're going."

articles.title: Freyr Alexandersson: Rosenborg boss 'overwhelmed' by Swansea City interest as new head coach
articles.summary: Rosenborg head coach Freyr Alexandersson confirmed he has spoken to the Championship side over the top job.
articles.body:
Rosenborg head coach Freyr Alexandersson admits he has found it "overwhelming" to be courted by managerless Swansea City and confirmed he has spoken to the Championship side.

Ashley Williams is currently interim boss at the Welsh club as they search for a permanent replacement for Vitor Matos following his shock departure to manage French side Strasbourg.

Icelander Alexandersson, 44, has only been in charge of Rosenborg since June but has already emerged as the front-runner for the Swansea job.

The Norwegian top-flight club were in danger of relegation when he was appointed, but are fourth with just three games remaining in the season, which concludes in mid-December.

"I can confirm that there is strong interest from Swansea," Alexandersson told Norsk rikskringkasting AS ahead of Saturday's crucial match against Molde, who are just one place behind Rosenborg in the Eliteserien table.

"I have heard from them (Swansea). I've never been in this situation before. Even just that is a bit overwhelming. I have strong emotions towards Rosenborg and particularly the players and the staff that I am working with, so that part is a bit difficult.

"But the interest itself from a club in England [sic] which I have said before, it is my dream to be a coach in English football.

"That in itself is something I find a bit interesting.

"I have no other plans than that I will be standing here tomorrow and hold training, have meetings and preparations ahead of Saturday's match, and be standing at the match on Saturday.

"That is what I can say now, because what has happened has happened very fast. And the last 24 hours I have only had focus on Rosenborg. I have had talks with (Rosenborg sporting director Alfred) Finnbogason, so I am only focusing on Saturday's match."

Williams to lead Swansea in south Wales derby

A badly timed shock - the story of Matos' Swans exit

Middlesbrough beat Swans to go point clear at top

Alexandersson previously worked for another Norwegian side, Brann, but was sacked earlier this year after 15 months in charge.

Prior to that, he was manager of Belgian side Kortrijk, who are a sister club of Cardiff City - Swansea's arch-rivals who they host in the south Wales derby this Sunday (12:00 GMT).

While Alexandersson admits he is unsure whether Swansea have made an official approach to Rosenborg for him, he did confirm he had spoken to the Welsh club.

When asked if he had been offered the Swansea job, Alexandersson replied: "Well, I cannot comment on that because Rosenborg and Swansea... I don't think there are negotiations even, I don't know what Alfred is saying about it, so I cannot comment.

"It is not me who has been hunting for a club. It is them who have come to me and that is of course a great honour to be the one they are hunting for. But Rosenborg... have said all the right things, handled it very, very well and we are trying to take this calmly because anything can happen. It is both ways.

He continued: "Yes (I have spoken to Swansea), but I have not heard from them since they talked with Alfred yesterday. Maybe if I have time this evening I will talk with them."

articles.title: Tonda Eckert: Southampton boss wants to close the chapter on 'Spygate' ahead of Middlesbrough reunion
articles.summary: Tonda Eckert speaks to Sky Sports News reporter Mark McAdam about 'Spygate' fallout, their points deduction and reunion with Middlesbrough. Watch Southampton vs Middlesbrough live on Sky Sports Football from 7.30pm on Friday night; kick-off 8pm.
articles.body:
It may be the understatement of the century, but it's not a huge surprise considering Tonda Eckert is a relatively understated man.

The storm of 'Spygate' is over, but the aftershock is still being felt. Southampton are sixth in the table, seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough ahead of their reunion on Friday night - live on Sky Sports .

Were it not for the four-point deduction, the gap would be smaller. Were it not for the entire controversy, the Saints would possibly be in the Premier League right now.

Eckert knows he broke the rules, and is thankful for the club and the support-base for backing him. Something that wouldn't have been easy after the ignominy of being kicked out of the play-offs.

"There have been some points, especially over the summer, where I think the club has made a commitment that not many clubs would have made," he admits.

"I'm very grateful, first of all, for the opportunity to step up in the first place, but also for the support over the summer. Obviously, that goes from everyone in the building to our supporters.

"This summer has been the biggest test we can possibly have in terms of the relationship between a football club and a fan base, and a manager and a fan base. I think the supporters have been great. It's been a tough period for them.

"Towards the end of last season, it was difficult to process for everyone because of the process we used. I would have wanted to address the supporters a little earlier, so it took almost two weeks before I got to speak to them.

"From there on, I think the commitment has been very clear. It started with the football club and some players who committed to the project.

"You could just sense, the closer we got to the season, that everyone wanted to leave that behind and show what we are about as a football club and how much joy we bring when we go on the pitch. We felt that throughout the summer and on the first day of training.

"To come out of that situation with new strength just shows what this football club is about. Now it's for us to look forward and make sure that we continue to do that.

"There was still some uncertainty for the first block of games, and you just need to find a way, for me and obviously for everyone else in the football club, to put that to the side. As soon as the season starts, you need to perform.

"Then, obviously, to close that chapter finally, we needed a decision from the club. I think that's helped us to close that chapter."

The uncertainty came from the FA investigation, which wasn't resolved until October. In the end he was given a fine and a suspended six-week ban.

"Obviously, it's never easy to work on a daily basis if you have some uncertainty, and that's not just for me," he says. "I think it's the same for everyone at the football club.

"But I think we found a way, even in the first block of games, to perform. There's always something going on in football, sometimes a little bit bigger and sometimes not as big, but you need to push that to the side and make sure you find a way to perform.

"Once the decision came, I think it was important for everyone that we could finally close that."

For Eckert and Southampton it is just about points on the board, now. Trying to make up the deficit they were dealt at the start of the season.

"Obviously, if you could choose, no one would choose to start the season on minus four points," he says. "That's what it is. I think we are strong enough to make our way forward in the table.

"You shouldn't underestimate us coming from behind. We've shown that we are able to chase teams down, and that's the job for this year.

"It's been important for us to get some points on the board early in the season. We are still not where we want to be towards the end, so we need to make sure we continue."

Last week, Southampton handed Eckert, still just 33, a contract extension until 2029 . They clearly feel he is their man to get them back to where they want to be.

"I think we've always been very open with our ambitions," he says. "There's no point in hiding that.

"I think the conditions are there to go up. It's never easy, but it's for us now to finish the job."

articles.title: Batalla campal en las gradas del Besiktas-Hapoel Beer Sheva por una bandera palestina
articles.standfirst: El partido se suspendió 20 minutos y un aficionado fue sacado en camilla
articles.summary: El partido se suspendió 20 minutos y un aficionado fue sacado en camilla
articles.body: una bandera palestina mostrada por los aficionados del Besiktas en la primera parte del partido ante los israelíes del Hapoel Beer Sheva provocó un tumulto en las radas del estadio de Batumi (Georgia), donde se está jugando el partido, en país neutral, por decisión de la UEFA. La intervención de la Policía georgiana supuso la interrupción del partido durante unos 20 minutos (iban 0-0) y una batalla campal contra los aficionados turcos. Transcurridos 25 minutos de juego y con empate a cero en el marcador (así se llegó al descanso), el colegiado del partido, el danés Morten Krogh, ordenó que los jugadores de ambos conjuntos abandonaran el campo por incidentes en la grada entre aficionados turcos y las fuerzas de seguridad. Ya antes de empezar el partido, los jugadores del Besiktas se negaron a estrechar la mano de sus rivales israelíes del Hapoel. El conflicto ha hecho que incluso clubes enemigos del Besiktas en Turquía, como el Fenerbahçe, hayan publicado un comunicado en apoyo de los hinchas del Besiktas desplazados hasta Georgia e involucrados en la pelea con la Policía local. De hecho, se ve en las imágenes cómo un aficionado turco es sacado en camilla del estadio por la gravedad de las heridas en el rifirrafe contra la Policía. El partido se ha reanudado luego. En un comunicado, el Besiktas acusó a las fuerzas de seguridad georgianas de emplear una fuerza "desproporcionada" contra los seguidores antes y durante el partido: "Condenamos enérgicamente a las fuerzas de seguridad por su uso de fuerza desproporcionada contra nuestros aficionados", manifestó el club. "También expresamos nuestros mejores deseos de una pronta recuperación a todos nuestros aficionados afectados por estos incidentes". El partido acabó finalmente con triunfo de los turcos con gol de Junior Olaitan en el minuto 75, y tras fallar Orkun Kökçü un penalti para los otomanos en el minuto 45+4. Este jugador se encargó de definir el choque (2-0) con un tanto en el 90'. Luego, East redujo el marcador con el 2-1 en el 93'.

articles.title: George Hemmings exclusive: Aston Villa prospect unfazed by rapid rise in Unai Emery's squad as he eyes next step
articles.summary: Sky Sports sits down with Aston Villa prospect George Hemmings to discuss his rise to the first team; Hemmings started for seven games before an injury curtailed progress; watch Ipswich vs Aston Villa live on Saturday Night Football, kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
The nineteen-year-old is quiet and reserved to start but soon settled into proceedings when quizzed on that atmosphere and what the experience was like.

"It was mad," he says with a smile on his face. "When we had the ball, you couldn't hear anything but whistling."

The mentality to take to an occasion such as that is largely expected by prospects in the modern game. A lofty standard set by the likes of Max Dowman and Rio Ngumoha.

But it does not mean we should lose sight of it.

For comparison, the journalist typing this was pulling on the ASDA shirt at the same age.

Hemmings, meanwhile, has been fast-tracked into the senior squad at Villa, thrust into an industry where the scrutiny and pressure is unmatched, and has impressed in the early stages of his career.

Unai Emery has an eye for talent and a knack for helping prospects tap into their potential. He wouldn't provide the platform for Hemmings if he didn't see something in the versatile midfielder.

"He is really good with me. He is always just looking for the best and always trying to improve me," he says when asked about the guidance Emery offers.

A quick glance out the window and you can see his team-mate, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, leaving. But it is two chairs and a spotlight for Hemmings, rather than an early exit.

His answers are short and snappy. A young prospect still getting to grips with the added responsibilities that come with being a Premier League footballer. But just like on the pitch, he takes it in his stride.

I move the conversation onto his quick rise into the first team. Following a summer of change at Villa Park, where Morgan Rogers, Ollie Watkins, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and more all departed, Hemmings was a shock inclusion in the starting line-up against Brighton on the opening day of the season.

A chastening 4-0 defeat would follow at the Amex Stadium, but in the brief spells of positive play from 10-man Villa on that day, Hemmings showed the flashes of talent that have caught the eye of Emery since day one.

He went on to start all seven games to begin 2026/27 before a knee injury curtailed his progress, with a first goal for the senior side still eluding him. He is yet to start a game since returning but Villa have reaffirmed their belief in the player after he penned a new five-year deal at the club.

"I am excited! It is five years, so I have a long time to improve myself and improve my game." I then pose the question of where he may see himself in his career in five years' time, where he adds: "We will have to see! I just have to keep working."

It is clear he is firmly in the plans of Emery and also revealed conversations about a potential loan exit before the season began never occurred.

"I always look at what is best for my career and once I saw that I could get a few games, I was always going to stay," he continued.

The 2-1 win against Coventry, arguably his strongest performance in a Villa shirt so far, offered a glimpse into what Emery is trying to coerce out of the young talent.

Tammy Abraham's opener at the CBS Arena came courtesy of a moment of real quality from Hemmings. His perfectly placed pass with the outside of his right boot dissected Premier League opposition and made the finish easy for his team-mate.

It offered an insight into the quality Villa hope he can one day produce regularly. But the celebrations also outlined why he is in the perfect environment for that necessary development.

Abraham quickly pointed to Hemmings and embraced his team-mate. Captain John McGinn arrived with a tap on the head, with Ross Barkley and Ibrahim Mbaye following suit.

The next opportunity to impress arrives on Saturday as Villa face Ipswich, live on Sky Sports , with a six-game winless run looming over the squad.

Hemmings was already around the squad prior to the major changes that occurred over the summer. Should he continue his current trajectory, he could become an increasingly important part of Emery's plans for years to come.

At 19, he still has plenty to learn but if his early steps in senior football are anything to go by, he is unlikely to be overawed by whatever the game can throw at him. It was a short encounter with Hemmings - but you can see why he is rated so highly at the club.

articles.title: El Vikingur confirma la muerte de Ingvar Jónsson
articles.standfirst: Fue convocado por Islandia para la Eurocopa 2016
articles.summary: Fue convocado por Islandia para la Eurocopa 2016
articles.body: Día de luto en el fútbol islandés. Tal y como informó el Vikingur en sus redes sociales, el guardameta Ingvar Jónsson, todavía en activo, falleció a la edad de 37 años víctima de un cáncer que le fue detectado a inicios de esta temporada. "Con profundo pesar y gran tristeza, comunicamos que nuestro querido amigo y compañero Ingvar Jónsson, portero del Víkingur, falleció el miércoles 25 de noviembre, en brazos de sus seres más cercanos. El club y todos los aficionados del Víkingur están junto a su familia y sus seres queridos. Les enviamos nuestras más sentidas condolencias", rezaba el comunicado publicado por el Vikingur en sus redes sociales. Ingvar Jónsson se encontraba jugando en el propio Vikingur desde febrero de 2020, cuando firmó libre procedente del Viborg danés. Hace justo una década, formó parte de la convocatoria de Islandia para la Eurocopa 2016... aunque no llegó a participar. Disputó ocho partidos a nivel internacional y dejó la selección en junio de 2022. Cinco veces campeón de la Liga islandesa, tres de Copa y otras tres de Supercopa, su último partido como profesional se remonta a mayo de 2026. Escasas semanas después, los médicos le detectaron que padecía cáncer y, menos de seis meses después, ha fallecido con apenas 37 años.

articles.title: AFC Champions League: Referee denies being drunk after half-time removal
articles.summary: A referee who was replaced at half-time of an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match denies he was drunk during the fixture.
articles.body:
Claims that a referee was drunk during an Asian Football Confederation (AFC) Champions League Two match are "entirely unfounded", officials say.

Syrian referee Hanna Hattab was replaced at half-time of the match between Iran's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates.

Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following what has been described as some erratic decision-making in the first half.

Iranian news agency ISNA quoted one club official as saying: "The referee was not in a normal state," and suggesting they would not have played on had the referee not been removed.

Accusations of drunkenness were also widely shared on social media.

But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has released a statement denying the allegation, saying he has been defamed and threatening legal action.

The fourth official took over for the second half, with Al Jazira winning the match.

Hattab said he will be "issuing an official statement that clarifies all the details and facts related to what happened".

Omani sports journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian competitions, claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus".

"He underwent a medical examination after the match and was not intoxicated, contrary to what has been circulating."

In their statement on the match, which was played in Asia's second tier continental competition, the Syrian Football Association backed Hattab.

"Following an assessment of his health, it has been confirmed - contrary to various claims circulating on social media - that the reports regarding his situation are entirely unfounded," they wrote.

"The Committee reiterates its unwavering support for him and is committed to thoroughly investigating all details and circumstances surrounding the incident."

articles.title: El Getafe queda herido de muerte en Georgia
articles.standfirst: Los de Bordalás siguen sin ganar en Europa tras otro K.O. ante el Iberia que le mantiene con un punto y le complica un poco más la clasificación
articles.summary: Los de Bordalás siguen sin ganar en Europa tras otro K.O. ante el Iberia que le mantiene con un punto y le complica un poco más la clasificación
articles.body: El Getafe no levanta cabeza en Europa. Los de Bordalás sumaron su tercera derrota en cuatro partidos y complican su clasificación para la siguiente ronda quedándose con tan solo un punto tras otro encuentro en el que se escenificaron los graves problemas ofensivos del equipo. Kobuladze dio el primer triunfo al Iberia 1999 georgiano en esta Conference en un duelo en el que los azulones jugaron más de media hora con diez futbolistas. Eso sí, los azulones salieron al campo buscando dominar con la posesión y siendo muy verticales por los costados y pronto tuvieron una doble ocasión en botas de Risco y de Satriano que acabó desbaratando el portero tras sendos remates dentro del área. Sin embargo, pasaban los minutos y los de Bordalás no encontraban el camino hacia la meta rival… y el contrario crecía. Así, superado el ecuador del primer acto, Kobuladze sorprendió tras un saque del guardameta aprovechando un desajuste en la zaga y, tras un primer remate tapado por Soria, abrir la lata a la segunda con todo a favor para desatar la locura en Tbilisi. Un mazazo para el equipo español, que lo intentó a arreones hasta el descanso -tuvo otra Satriano, con un disparo muy centrado- pero que se volvió a ver por debajo en el marcador en Europa antes de irse al vestuario. Tras el receso, José Bordalás tomó cartas en el asunto y metió a Enes Unal, Mangala y Zaid en busca de una reacción. Sin embargo, los georgianos pusieron a prueba a David Soria en dos ocasiones nada más empezar. El guardameta se lució para evitar los goles de Dzagania y de Kardava… antes de otro mazazo en forma de tarjeta roja. Mangala, que había entrado en la segunda mitad, vio dos amarillas en apenas tres minutos tras un entrada, primero, en la que levantó mucho el pie y golpeó con la planta al rival y, después, tras frenar un contragolpe golpeando con la cadera a un rival a la altura del centro del campo que le costó otra cartulina cuanto menos rigurosa. El Geta estaba desesperado, no se encontraba… y se le puso el asunto más cuesta arriba todavía. Entraron Francho y Andrés para ir con todo hasta el final, lo que provocó que el Geta se volcase ante la meta rival. Las llegadas se multiplicaban, es cierto, pero la única clara fue de Gudelj, con un derechazo desde la frontal que sacó Jinjolava bajo palos cuando apenas quedaban 20 minutos de batalla, con el Iberia replegado esperando un contragolpe o un mínimo error para poner la puntilla. Un plan que acabó siendo exitoso ante la desesperación getafense, que volvía a toparse una y otra vez con un muro. Así se llegó al final, con el conjunto madrileño buscando a la desesperada algo que no encontró y con el cuadro georgiano mostrándose firme y solidario en el esfuerzo para meterse al bolsillo sus primeros tres puntos. Por el contrario, el Geta se queda a tres puntos del 24º puesto que daría acceso al playoff y con dos finales en el horizonte: ante el Inter D’Escaldes andorrano (colista con cero puntos) en el Coliseum… y frente al Ajax en Ámsterdam. Herido de muerte, pero todavía vivo.

articles.title: El Celta se hunde en un déjà vu
articles.standfirst: Por tercer partido seguido en Europa en Balaídos se deja remontar un 1-0 y acaba perdiendo
articles.summary: Por tercer partido seguido en Europa en Balaídos se deja remontar un 1-0 y acaba perdiendo
articles.body: Aspas se quedó un año más para pasárselo bien, para disfrutar de Balaídos en Europa. Y la verdad es que la temporada del Celta no está siendo muy divertida, ni el fin de semana, ni entre semana, ni en casa ni fuera. Si a eso le sumas que visitaba Vigo el líder de la Europa League, un Bournemouth que llevaba cuatro victorias en cuatro partidos en la competición y nueve encuentros seguidos ganando, pues la noche requería una tonelada de magia. Y a Iago le queda, pero no tanta. El Celta salió a merendarse a los 'cherries', que se empadronaron en su área desde el inicio y apenas inquietaron en el primer tiempo. Los celestes buscaron el gol desde el vamos y Pablo Durán marcó en claro fuera de juego en el minuto 11, tras cazar un rechace en el área, en lo que fue el aperitivo de la jugada del 1-0. Driouech metió un balón al área y al señor de 39 años que lleva el 10 del Celta no se le ocurrió otra cosa que clavarse una chilena. Di Gregorio se lanzó abajo y despejó y Aspas, en vez de levantarse con una mano en la espalda por el lumbago, se puso en pie de un salto, pidió otra vez que le pasaran el balón, dejó roto a Alex Scott con un recorte, se dibujó un perímetro despejado de un metro sin rivales y ahí Iago es trampa, es como un juego antiguo de recreativas en el que sabías que si le pegabas desde ahí y al palo largo, era gol siempre. Y le pegó al palo largo y fue gol. El partido se le puso aún más de cara al Celta con la expulsión de Diakité en el 23', por pegarle un pisotón en el tobillo a Droiuech. Fue tan claro que Osmers, que había sacado amarilla en directo, necesitó pocos segundos en el monitor para cambiar su decisión y expulsarle. Aún pudo sacarle más jugo el equipo celeste a la primera mitad, pero a Pablo Durán le anularon otro gol por fuera de juego antes del descanso. Parecía una tarde tranquila en Vigo, pero ni el Bournemouth ni el Celta están como están por casualidad. Tyler Adams entró tras el descanso y nada más empezar la segunda parte metió un centro al área que Álvaro Rodríguez peleó y cabeceó a la altura de su propio ombligo en un escorzo dificilísimo pero efectivo, porque batió a Radu. Y entonces, como cuando te despiertan en un espectáculo de hipnosis, el Celta revivió de golpe todos sus males de la temporada, no recordó cómo había jugado en la primera parte y el Bournemouth dejó de hacer la gallina y empezó a someter a los de Giráldez. Con uno menos y en un momento en el que el Celta había recuperado el dominio del partido, llegó el picotazo definitivo. Una jugada a toda velocidad del equipo de Rose en la que los celestes pidieron falta sobre Carreira acabó en el área y en los pies de Rayan, que remató con la zurda, de primeras, para dejar a Radu haciendo la estatua. Por tercer partido seguido en la Europa League en Balaídos el Celta empezó ganando. Por tercer partido seguido en la Europa League en Balaídos el Celta acabó perdiendo 1-2. Un bucle perpetuo que deja a los de Giráldez al borde de la eliminación y con caras larguísimas.

articles.title: El Bernabéu, de concierto en concierto
articles.standfirst: Los blancos, con 30 goles a favor y siete en contra y pleno de triunfos, los mejores tanto en la Liga como en la Champions en su estadio
articles.summary: Los blancos, con 30 goles a favor y siete en contra y pleno de triunfos, los mejores tanto en la Liga como en la Champions en su estadio
articles.body: José Ángel Sánchez, director general del Real Madrid, confirmó en la última Asamblea que ya no hay impedimento legal para que los conciertos vuelvan al Bernabéu. A la espera de que esto suceda, la realidad es que la afición se consuela bastante bien con lo que ve cada jornada de Liga o de Champions en el Bernabéu. El Madrid ha ido a más y ha logrado convertir su estadio en un fortín. Es ya el único equipo de la Liga que cuenta todos sus partidos en casa por triunfos, con 18 puntos, y también es el máximo goleador, con 30 dianas por solo siete en contra. El Madrid suma defensivamente cifras de campeón, con solo 11 goles en contra en 13 jornadas de Liga, solo superado también esta faceta por los rojiblancos con un tanto menos en contra. Pero el Madrid es el mejor equipo también en casa en la Champions. No hay nadie que haya hecho ya pleno en la competición tras el pinchado de esta última jornada del PSG de Luis Enrique. Cinco tantos al PSV, cuatro al Leipzig y dos al Inter en el primer partido en casa, lo que muestra sin duda le evolución positiva del equipo. En Liga, el Madrid ha alcanzado ya los cuatro goles en cuatro partidos (Real Sociedad, Málaga, Rayo y Sevilla). El equipo se ha dejado el liderato lejos del Bernabéu con las derrotas ante el Atlético y el Betis. Suma ya diez triunfos consecutivos. Jugar en el Bernabéu se había convertido para el Madrid en una reválida permanente. Pese a que el club atribuía los pitos a unos pocos y a una campaña orquestada, la realidad es que han ido a menos cuando el equipo ha empezado a ganar y a mostrar compromiso. La campaña pasada se tocó fondo con el primer partido de Arbeloa en Liga tras caer esa semana en Copa. La grada se levantó como nunca y la temporada acabaría de nuevo en blanco con una grada a disgusto. En esta temporada, el ambiente que se respiraba era una de las cosas que más inquietaba a Mourinho, que siempre ha respetado a la afición para protestar pero les ha recordado que es más fácil jugar con el ambiente a favor. El luso también notó un ambiente algo más hostil, quizá producto de lo que ha pasado estas dos últimas temporadas, pero ha logrado la paz en casa.

articles.title: Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth: Rayan gets winner as Cherries become first English side ever to win first five games in major European competition
articles.summary: Report from the Europa League game between Celta Vigo and Bournemouth at Estadio Abanca-Balaidos; Iago Aspas put home side in front before Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan struck to earn the Cherries a historic victory as Bournemouth extended their winning run to 10 matches in all competitions
articles.body:
It was a club-record-extending 10th successive win for Bournemouth in all competitions, with the victory also marking the first time an English club have won their first five matches in major European competition.

Veteran former Liverpool striker Iago Aspas put the home side in front in style in the first half, before Bournemouth were reduced to 10 men when Bafode Diakite was sent off for a late challenge.

But Alvaro Rodriguez equalised early in the second half, with substitute Rayan coming on to score a late winner to give Bournemouth an unlikely win.

Bournemouth were fortunate not to go behind after 10 minutes, with an offside flag chalking off Pablo Duran's poke home from close-range.

But the Cherries fell behind 10 minutes later when record Celta Vigo goalscorer Aspas scored a screamer.

The 39-year-old had seen an overhead kick saved well by Michele Di Gregorio, but he picked up the ball on the right side of the area in the second phase of play, before cutting inside to curl past the goalkeeper and into the far corner off the post.

Things went from bad to worse for Bournemouth moment later when Diakite saw a yellow card upgraded to a red after a VAR check following a late challenge on Couhaib Driouech.

Tyler Adams replaced Justin Kluivert at half-time and the tactical switch drew an instant reward when Alvaro Rodriguez glanced home Amine Adli's cross to get Bournemouth back on level terms.

James Hill then drew a fine save from Ionut Radu - who is the only player ever to play for both clubs - before Di Gregorio was called into action at the other end to divert a long-range Aspas strike away.

But three Bournemouth substitutes combined for a late winner.

Adrien Truffert stole possession and broke before finding Marcus Tavernier the area. He laid the ball off for Rayan to sweep home and seal victory as Marco Rose's side made more history with a brilliant win at the Estadio Abanca-Balaidos.

11: GOAL RULED OUT! Duran follows up on an initial shot from Driouech to bundle home but is ruled off-side.

19: GOAL! Veteran striker and former Liverpool man Aspas scores a screamer to give Celta Vigo the lead!

25: RED CARD! Diakite is sent off after a VAR check for a late challenge on Driouech!

30: GOAL RULED OUT! Celta have the ball in the back of the net again, but Duran is again denied by an off-side flag.

39: SAVE! Kluivert shoots from a very tight angle - but it is well saved by Radu in the Celta Vigo goal.

46: GOAL! Rodriguez scores with a glancing header from close-range after a beautiful cross from the right-hand side by Adli.

60: SAVE! Scott goes for goal from a free kick from a tight angle but Radu has it covered.

63: SAVE! Hill has a go from range but the goalkeeper tips over.

73: SAVE! Aspas shoots from the edge of the area and Di Gregorio gets down well to save.

78: GOAL! What a turnaround! Rayan sweeps home to give Bournemouth the lead!

Everyone was motivated - Adli hails Cherries character in win at Celta

"Now we're enjoying a good run of form and things are going well for us," said Bournemouth midfielder Amine Adli. "We're in a good moment with confidence and a positive atmosphere.

"We're trying to maintain this energy and all the good things we're doing on the pitch, and keep reproducing them in every game."

articles.title: La última heroicidad de Shengelia aleja a Grecia del Mundial
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot, que había perdido a su abuela en las últimas horas, disputó 44 minutos tras haber jugado este miércoles en Dubái y, con 25 puntos y 11 rebotes, fue clave en el triunfo de Georgia en la prórroga (88-92)
articles.summary: El ala-pívot, que había perdido a su abuela en las últimas horas, disputó 44 minutos tras haber jugado este miércoles en Dubái y, con 25 puntos y 11 rebotes, fue clave en el triunfo de Georgia en la prórroga (88-92)
articles.body: El compromiso de Tornike Shengelia con su selección no tiene límites. El ala-pívot georgiano lo ha demostrado muchas veces con esfuerzos físicos que le han jugar partidos en días consecutivos con viajes de por medio. Yendo un paso más allá, jugó en Atenas tocado mentalmente tras conocer el fallecimiento de su abuela. Su última heroicidad dejó a Georgia cerca del Mundial y a Grecia, bastante lejos. Shengelia jugo este miércoles en Dubái con su equipo ante el Partizan en la Euroliga. No estuvo bien. Hizo dos puntos en 22 minutos. Poco más de 24 horas después comenzaba un partido clave en el OAKA ante Grecia. Y allí estaba él para estar en pista durante 43:48 minutos, pues hubo prórroga. Decisivo, como siempre que juega su selección, sumó 25 puntos, 11 rebotes y cinco asistencias. "Salió y jugó con el alma. Por todo el mundo. Siempre jugaré para Georgia, pero en este partido realmente estaba jugando para Toko. Quería ganar este partido por él", dijo emocionado su compañero Duda Sanadze, que fue quien hizo público el fallecimiento de la abuela de Shengelia. Georgia pudo ganar el partido antes de la prórroga, pero una falta de Andronikashvili a Dorsey en el último segundo le dio tres tiros libres al nacionalizado heleno. Falló uno y el choque se fue al tiempo extra. Ahí, los locales se plantaron 88-81 a falta de 57 segundos. Lo tenían hecho y lo dejaron escapar. Recibieron un parcial de 0-11 con una decisiva flagrante de Kostas Antetokounmpo incluida. El máximo anotador de los georgianos fue el nacionalizado Marcquise Reed, que se fue a los 30 puntos. "Hemos perdido contra dos jugadores", dijo el seleccionador griego Vassilis Spanoulis. Por su equipo, Konstantinos Mitoglou hizo 19+8 y Dorsey llegó a los 17, pero con malos porcentajes de tiro (3/12). Con la derrota los helenos tienen muy cuesta arriba su clasificación para el Mundial. Marchan con un balance de 4-5 y la tercera plaza, la última que da billete, está a dos triunfos a falta de dos jornadas. Su próxima cita es en Santiago de Compostela este domingo ante una selección española que, de ganar, tendrá el billete casi asegurado. Para Grecia, tras la última gesta de Shengelia, es una final.

articles.title: D.J. Jacobs Commits to Miami After Ohio State Decommitment, What to Know About 5-Star EDGE
articles.summary: D.J. Jacobs, the No. 2 overall recruit in the 2027 class, wasted little time in making a decision on his future after backing out of his commitment to Ohio State on Thursday.
articles.body:
D.J. Jacobs, the No. 2 overall recruit in the 2027 class, wasted little time in making a decision on his future after backing out of his commitment to Ohio State on Thursday.

Jacobs committed to Miami, fulfilling a dream of his.

"I always grew up a fan of Miami," Jacobs told Rivals' Chad Simmons . "Mark Richt played there, and he's my godfather. I love the staff, and everything is great at Miami. They've always been up there for me. As a kid, I dreamed of playing for Miami."

Jacobs noted that the coaching played a role in his decision.

"They have a great staff and I get to play for Jason Taylor," Jacobs said, per Simmons. "He's an awesome coach and one of the best to ever do it. Coach Taylor is a great person and a great coach. It is insane what he does with his guys. He prepares them for the NFL."

Jacobs also made it clear that he has a lot of respect for head coach Mario Cristobal as well.

"Coach Mario Cristobal is too. I love him. I've said from the beginning that the people in the building matter to me, and Miami has some of the best," Jacobs said, per Simmons. "He has gotten Miami back to the top. Coach Cristobal has built Miami back up."

Per 247Sports' Tom Loy and ESPN's Eli Lederman , Jacobs decommitted from Ohio State and will no longer attend Saturday's game against Michigan as was previously scheduled.

Lederman added Jacobs visited Tennessee last weekend for its matchup with LSU. Georgia was also considered among the top contenders for the Blessed Trinity Catholic High School standout.

Jacobs is a 5-star prospect and No. 1 EDGE player in the 2027 recruiting class, per 247Sports' composite rankings . He originally committed to Ohio State in December 2025.

Georgia, Miami and Texas A&M were among the other schools Jacobs was considering at that time.

According to Lederman, Jacobs had a revenue-sharing agreement with Ohio State as part of his commitment that would have paid him more than $2 million annually.

Even with Jacobs' decommitment, Ohio State still has the No. 7 recruiting class in the country for next season. Lederman did note other programs are "circling" that group with the Buckeyes struggling right now.

Jacobs' move comes as Ohio State has lost three of its last four games. The Buckeyes' four losses overall are their most in a single season since 2011.

Among Jacobs' potential suitors, Georgia has a personal connection to the family. His father, David Jacobs, played on the Bulldogs defensive line from 1999 to 2002.

Georgia is currently ranked No. 1 in the College Football Playoff Top 25. Tennessee is at No. 5, followed by Miami at No. 7.

In the end, however, Jacobs opted to commit to Miami, a team that was playing for a national championship last season and could earn a spot in the College Football Playoff again this year.

articles.standfirst: Derrotas del Celta y la Real Sociedad en Europa League y del Getafe en Conference
articles.summary: Derrotas del Celta y la Real Sociedad en Europa League y del Getafe en Conference
articles.body: Hace 24 horas España se vanagloriaba de la gran jornada en Champions, con cinco victorias de los cinco representantes de la Liga en la máxima competición continental. Pero este jueves todo lo que era alegría se ha transformado en decepción. La tarde empezó con las derrotas del Celta en Balaídos ante el Bournemouth (1-2) y del Getafe en Georgia frente al Iberia (1-0). Dos resultados que, además, complican la supervivencia de ambos equipos en la Europa League y en la Conference, respectivamente. La noche parecía ir mejor, porque la Real Sociedad empezó ganando ante el Crystal Palace en Inglaterra... pero los londinenses le dieron la vuelta al marcador, acabaron derrotando por 2-1 a los de Matarazzo y le pusieron el sello al jueves negro del fútbol español en Europa. Todo esto afecta, claro, a las aspiraciones de España de volver a mandar cinco equipos a la próxima Champions League. Primero, porque este jueves no se ha sumado nada después de un martes y un miércoles perfectos. Y segundo, porque si los equipos españoles caen eliminados, lo que sumen los que se clasifiquen se seguirá dividiendo entre ocho para hacer las cuentas. Si caen tan pronto uno o dos clubes de la Liga, las matemáticas complican mucho la candidatura española a ese premio por rendimiento de la UEFA. El drama del jueves hace caer de forma drástica a España en el ránking de Rendimiento Deportivo de la temporada de UEFA, la que otorga esas dos plazas extra para la próxima Champions a las dos ligas que mejores datos obtengan. España, tras las tres derrotas comentadas, cae hasta la séptima plaza con 9.125 puntos, por detrás de Inglaterra (10.500), Portugal (9.900), Bélgica (9.600), Alemania (9.571), Turquía (9.500) e Italia (9.214).

articles.title: Crystal Palace 2-1 Real Sociedad: Thomas Frank earns first win as Eagles boss with Europa League comeback victory
articles.summary: Match report as Thomas Frank earns his first win as Crystal Palace manager; Mamadou Sarr gave Real Sociedad the lead after a dominant opening hour; Jon Martin was sent off and Jean-Philippe Mateta scored from the penalty spot to level; Dwight McNeill score the winner
articles.body:
The Dane lost his opening game to Coventry at the weekend, but saw the heart and fight he will need from his side as they picked up their second win in the competition this season.

For 70 minutes, Sociedad dominated at Selhurst Park, with Dean Henderson needed to make a string of saves. They finally made the breakthrough when Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr tapped home from Job Ochieng's cross.

But the game turned out of nowhere as Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty and Jon Martin was sent off. He picked up a second yellow card for holding Jean-Philippe Mateta round the middle, with the striker expertly dispatching the spot kick to level for the Eagles.

The confidence surged in the hosts - backed by the famous atmosphere at Selhurst Park - and it was a well-worked second that put them ahead.

Yeremy Pino's cross was cleared to Jorgen Strand Larsen at the back post, who hit an overhead kick. It wasn't on target, but it did bobble into the six-yard box for the incoming Dwight McNeil, who slid to poke home.

Crystal Palace could have wrapped up the points in a topsy-turvy end after they were awarded another penalty. Carlos Soler was penalised for handball, but Pino's effort was well-saved by Unai Marrero.

The win catapults Crystal Palace into 12th place in the league phase table, just two from the top eight, and gives them a huge boost ahead of another key clash against Hull on Super Sunday . Real Sociedad have slid down into 27th.

35: SAVE! Dean Henderson has to be alert as Goncalo Guedes strikes, but the goalkeeper is down to push it away.

38: SAVE! A wonderful pass from Mikel Oyarzabal to release Guedes, but his shot is pushed away by Henderson.

45: ALMOST! A Chris Richards long throw is pinged into the box, Axel Disasi nods it on for Jean-Philippe Mateta - but the Frenchman's own header goes wide.

52: SAVE! OVER! Henderson pushes away Gorrotxategi's shot before the rebound is skied into the stands.

67: GOAL! Sarr taps home after Ochieng's low pass.

71: PENALTY CRYSTAL PALACE! RED CARD! Martin has his arms wrapped around Mateta for far too long and picks up a second yellow card.

73: GOAL! Mateta fires home the penalty to level for Crystal Palace.

82: GOAL! McNeil turns home from Strand Larsen's overhead kick to put the Eagles ahead.

90: PENALTY! Crystal Palace are awarded a second penalty for a Soler handball, but Pino has his effort saved.

90+7: SAVE! Henderson pushes away a shot from Oskarsson to keep Sociedad from a late leveller.

Frank hopes Europa win can be turning point in Palace's season

Crystal Palace manager Thomas Frank to TNT Sport on if the win can be a turning point: "I surely hope so. You can't underestimate a win, what that gives the group, what they're feeling.

"I think there was more positives than negatives from this performance, but still a lot we need to work on, and to keep working on.

"It's a fantastic feeling to get the win in every aspect here at home and in the circumstances that it's a season that hasn't been living up to everything we expected, so the confidence is maybe not at the highest.

"The ability to come from 1-0 behind and then go to win the game, the mentality and the belief in the players was really good.

"We're playing a very good team, they're fifth in LaLiga, they're very good on the ball. Not everything was perfect in the first half, but the willingness to suffer together and defend together was there, that was good, then we built a little bit more into the second half."

McNeil: Frank has bought energy and confidence

Crystal Palace goalscorer Dwight McNeil to TNT Sport on what Frank has bought to the club: "It's like an energy, a belief. He keeps telling us how good as players we are, but now we're just putting it out on the pitch and we did that tonight.

"We knew it was going to be a tough game but we stuck in there, especially going down 1-0 and then the big man [Mateta] scoring to get us back into the game and then we go on from there."

In response, Frank said: "It's easy to bring energy and the confidence, but what really moves the needle is that you get over the line and get some wins.

"In the last five minutes, I think we all almost were about to get a heart attack because it went both ways, back-to-back. That's also part of the confidence and also we should have controlled that game against 10, but it's football, it's emotions, it's everything."

Flashes of the 'old' Crystal Palace in Europa win

Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh : "Perhaps one of the most surprising aspects of Crystal Palace this season has been a lack of fight and desire.

"Under Pierre Sage, the team looked disjointed and out of sorts. You did not always see the same determination and sheer-mindedness that has seen the Eagles achieve beyond their wildest dreams over the last few years.

"But we saw that again on Thursday - the Palace of last season, of 'old' perhaps, is still there. To come from behind against a team of Real Sociedad's quality is impressive, and it hinged on one moment. Some fans might say it is about time things started turning in Palace's favour this season.

"They had certainly ridden their luck until that point. Frank very quickly must eradicate the mistakes in and out of possession. Too many sloppy moments allowed Sociedad onto the ball and to have a shot. They were certainly victims of their own lack of precision - Palace might not be so fortunate next time.

"But what the final 20 minutes and result will bring them is a huge boost in confidence that must be channelled towards the Premier League. Frank said in his pre-match press conference that he knows he will be judged on league results and he's right - now it's time to start getting some."

articles.title: Bordalás: "Mis equipos eran reconocibles y en este momento es justo todo lo contrario"
articles.standfirst: El técnico, muy decepcionado tras un batacazo con el que nadie contaba
articles.summary: El técnico, muy decepcionado tras un batacazo con el que nadie contaba
articles.body: Bordalás no puso paños calientes a la derrota en sus declaraciones a Movistar nada más terminar el encuentro. El técnico azulón mostró su disgusto por un KO que, a su juicio, entierra cualquier opción de clasificación en Europa. Sensaciones tras el partido: "Derrota difícil, momento duro. El equipo ha venido con la intención de conseguir una victoria. Necesitábamos un triunfo y no hemos sido capaces". Opciones de seguir adelante: "Las posibilidades pasaban por conseguir una victoria hoy y se disiparon todas las posibilidades. A partir de ahora hay que pensar en LaLiga, donde también la situación es complicada". Próximos partidos: "No podemos seguir acumulando decepciones porque ya son muchas lo que se ha ido acumulando. Durante estas temporadas mis equipos eran muy reconocibles y en este momento es todo lo contrario. No se parece nada a lo que han sido mis equipos". Problemas con el gol: "Tenemos un déficit muy grande y, bueno, de hecho, nos faltan jugadores que dominen el uno contra uno, que tengan velocidad. Cualquier equipo hoy tiene velocidad, de medio campo hacia adelante".

articles.title: Konaté, en el nombre del padre
articles.standfirst: El central se hizo futbolista para que Hamady Konaté, enfermo y fallecido hace un año, pudiera verle por televisión
articles.summary: El central se hizo futbolista para que Hamady Konaté, enfermo y fallecido hace un año, pudiera verle por televisión
articles.body: Ibrahima Konaté se ha consolidado en el Real Madrid de Mourinho. Atrás queda su momento más complicado de su carrera, tras la muerte de su padre en enero de 2026 y seis meses antes la de su compañero en el Liverpool Diogo Jota. Dos golpes en la vida que le afectaron, en medio de una decisión trascendental para su vida: no renovar con el Liverpool para dar por concluida su etapa en Anfield y da el salto al Real Madrid. Konaté ha salido a flote con su receta de siempre, la que le inculcaron sus cinco hermanos mayores: Diawoye, Sirima, Mamby, Sikou et Moriba. Sus padres siempre estuvieron alejados del fútbol y se focalizaron solo en la educación de su hijo. Su madre no iba porque tenía miedo que le pasara algo a su niño y el padre se sorprendió una de las pocas veces que vio un entrenamiento por el canal de televisión del Liverpool. "Haces esto todos los días, debes estar muerto", le dijo su padre. Sus hermanos nunca le pidieron un euro, pero fueron sus mejores consejeros, también para esta última decisión. Que su padre no fuera a los estadios, sin embargo, no respondía a su falta de apego al fútbol. "Mi padre estaba enfermo -reveló en 2022 en Bein Sports- y nunca ha podido verme jugar en el campo, así que pensé que me tenía que hacer profesional para que me pudiera ver al menos por la tele". El ahora jugador del Real Madrid lleva grabado este mensaje de su padre, de origen maliense, que desveló en Ouest France: "No os peleéis, ni entre vosotros ni con los demás. Sed humildes. Y si mañana alguno de vosotros se desvía del camino, recordádselo enseguida. Manteneos unidos y volved a lo esencial. Algún día, yo ya no estaré aquí. Vuestra madre tampoco. Conservad esa fuerza entre vosotros". Sus hermanos mayores forjaron su carácter, humilde, trabajador, líder y bromista, también en el vestuario. Bastó una mañana en la que el jugador, ya en la élite, regresó con uno de sus hermanos a su barrio de infancia en París. Los hermanos le animaron en su momento a darse lujos, pero eso no implicaba descuidar los detalles. Ibrahima llegó con un traje de lujo al barrio La Roquette, en el distrito 11 de París. "Ibou, solo se te ve a ti, pero en cambio no eres tú. No necesitas eso. Siempre que vuelvas, intenta ser como la gente que te rodea". Konaté ha salido a flote y no ha sido fácil. Pese a que ya en el Mundial se vio muy recuperado, fue el cuarto central de Deschamps. Solo quince minutos ante Noruega y la primera parte en el tercer y cuarto puesto con Inglaterra. Aterrizó en el Madrid y no arrancó con el brillo de este último mes. Era cuestión de tiempo y de confianza que le ha dado Mourinho. Con Militao intentando salir de su última grave lesión, Konaté se ha hecho fuerte en el centro de la zaga, también por delante de Rüdiger. El entrenador mantiene otro perfil de central para su acompañante con Huijsen. El papel del defensa duro, físicamente infranqueable e intimidador, se lo ha llevado por ahora por delante del brasileño y el alemán. El ex del Liverpool solo se ha quedado sin jugar un partido de Liga, ante el Málaga, en los otros doce ha sido titular y no se ha perdido un minuto. Ahora la continuidad da sus frutos, como se vio ante el PSV, partido que arrancó en el banquillo para salir tras el descanso junto a Huijsen. Y es que en Champions es donde más ha rotado, dos partidos sin jugar y otros dos titular al margen de este último.

articles.title: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood’s status for Ohio State game gets huge update
articles.summary: Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood returned to the starting lineup last weekend and helped secure bowl eligibility. An injury then raised questi...
articles.body:
Michigan Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood returned to the starting lineup last weekend and helped secure bowl eligibility. An injury then raised questions about his availability for Saturday's regular-season finale vs. the Ohio State Buckeyes.

Head coach Kyle Whittingham named Underwood the starter on Monday, provided he made it through the week without a setback. Michigan football subsequently listed the sophomore as questionable on its initial Big Ten availability report.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Thursday on X, formerly Twitter, that a hamstring injury limited Underwood in practice earlier this week. The sophomore is expected to be available and remains in line to start against Ohio State barring a setback.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Underwood made his first start since October 17 in Michigan's 18-16 triple-overtime win over the UCLA Bruins. He completed 11 of 24 passes for 127 yards and a touchdown, then found tight end Jalen Hoffman for the winning two-point conversion.

True freshman Tommy Carr started during a midseason stretch before Underwood reclaimed the job against UCLA. The Wolverines turned back to their sophomore signal-caller after he had gone more than a month between starts.

The victory came at Michigan Stadium and secured bowl eligibility for the Wolverines. They enter their final Big Ten game at 3-5 in conference play before heading to a bowl in Whittingham's first season.

The former No. 1 overall recruit has thrown for 1,077 yards, six touchdowns and six interceptions in nine appearances this season. He has added 230 rushing yards and two scores.

Michigan heads to Columbus at 6-5, while Ohio State sits at 7-4 after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska. The rivals kick off at noon ET on FOX at Ohio Stadium. Underwood remains in line to start if he avoids a setback before kickoff.

articles.title: Big 10 Pick 6: Ending on a High Note
articles.summary: A season of disorder continued last week with crazy results like UW and Nebraska beating Indiana and Ohio State outright. The outcomes have left me at a disa...
articles.body:
A season of disorder continued last week with crazy results like UW and Nebraska beating Indiana and Ohio State outright. The outcomes have left me at a disappointing 34-39-1. We can only hope that the entropy continues for another week with the Dawgs heading to Autzen with a chance to redeem a frustrating season.

The Ducks looked dead in the water after losing to Illinois. They were 4-3 with an anemic offense, and injured QB, and seemingly no postseason hopes. They fired their offensive coordinator and it has been off to the races ever since, with four straight wins, including three over teams with winning records. The problem for most of the season was that the offense was simply too erratic. They could make big plays with Dakorien Moore, but their trademark short passing game from the Will Stein era was not getting consistent first downs. That tendency has improved under new OC Jay Johnson and the Ducks are scoring 30+ in every game. Dylan Raiola has cleaned up the turnover problems he had earlier in the year and the running game is back on track. The Husky defense has done a good job forcing turnovers through the season, as well as at limiting big plays. Given that those are the two areas where Oregon has struggled at points in the season, there's at least a chance that the Dawgs could pose more of a problem for the rejuvenated Ducks offense.

On the other side, Oregon's defense has been solid for virtually the full season. Even in the losses to UCLA and Illinois, they gave up only 17 and 21 points. It was really only the shock defeat to Oklahoma State where the defense struggled. Washington's offense has improved itself in the second half of the year by leaning into what Demond Williams can do well- run the ball and freelance in the passing game. Both the surprise wins against very good Nebraska and Indiana defenses relied on Williams creating something out of nothing. There will be missed deep balls and open receivers he doesn't see, but if the Huskies have a chance to pull the upset, it will be because Williams made an excellent defense uncomfortable. I think he will do it, but not often enough to keep up with an Oregon offense that is playing so much better over the last month.

Nebraska has reversed its standard late season collapse with consecutive wins over Rutgers and Ohio St. Anthony Collandrea has kept the offense function against good defenses, even if it looks workmanlike at times. Stylistically, these teams are mirror images of one another- they keep the ball on the ground, slow the game down, and keep the score low with big, physical defenses. I think Nebraska has a slightly more balanced offense, but I also think Iowa gets some home field advantage.

Statistically, I'd be willing to write off Minnesota, but they keep putting up results that don't square with the underlying numbers. They're outside the top 100 nationally in EPA per pass AND rush. Unless you have Georgia's defense, that's a recipe for disaster. And yet, the Gophers have wins over Iowa, Washington, and, most recently, Northwestern. For as many times as Wisconsin has been ready to fire Luke Fickell, he has them firmly entrenched as a respectable team this year. Maybe PJ Fleck's horseshoe come into play again, but Wisconsin looks like the better option here.

It's exceptionally rare for this game to matter so little. You might get one team down for a year, but rarely both. Ohio St last came into the game with four losses in 2011 and 2004. In those seasons, Michigan was on its way to the Sugar and Rose Bowls, respectively. The Buckeyes have been off since Julian Sayin was injured, but the defense is as much of a problem as the offense. They've given up 30+ in three of the last four games. Unlike Oregon, Michigan did not get an immediate bump from replacing their OC. I still believe in Michigan's defense, but without more offensive firepower, it's going to be hard to keep up.

You don't have to be a UCLA alum to feel for how their season has played out. Bob Chesney immediately turned around a team that has languished for ages. They battled through the loss of their QB and kept rolling. Unfortunately, they lost their backup QB and their first game last week in the Big House. Perhaps with a week to prepare, Madden Iamaleava can keep the offense moving, but it's hard to see them keeping up with a legitimately good USC offense.

I wrote last week that I can't hold it against Northwestern that they lost three straight to Oregon, Iowa, and Ohio St. Then they lost a fourth straight to Minnesota. Illinois is the abnormal Big 10 team with a better offense than defense. It might be just what Northwestern needs to score some points and end the regular season on a high note.

articles.title: ‘What a team’ – Marco Rose after Bournemouth make it ten wins in a row with comeback Europa League victory
articles.summary: Marco Rose hailed Bournemouth’s spirit and energy after they came from behind with 10 men to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 and make it ten wins in a row in all competi...
articles.body:
Marco Rose hailed Bournemouth's spirit and energy after they came from behind with 10 men to beat Celta Vigo 2-1 and make it ten wins in a row in all competitions.

Bournemouth were a goal down and a player short after Bafode Diaktie's first-half sending off but fought back after the break to secure an impressive victory thanks to goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan, with Rose delighted by the character shown by his side.

"What a team, what a spirit, what an energy," he said.

"I'm really proud after being one player less, 1-0 down."

Rose also praised the way his players adapted tactically, singling out David Brooks for his performance in an unfamiliar defensive role.

"I said to Ty [Adams], sometimes it's not about tactics and formations and stuff like this," he said.

"Brooksy did a great job when we got one player less, he played just right defender like he played it for 10 years.

"We changed in the right moment, everyone did his job on a really high level."

Rose felt Bournemouth's equaliser after half-time shifted the momentum of the contest and praised his side for continuing to push for the winner.

"We created the momentum after the half-time with the first goal and we were just relentless," he said.

"We never stopped to believe in this win and that's why big, big, big congratulations to the team."
